newsitem.title: USA: New money boosts stock fund assets to $2 trillion in May.
newsitem.headline: New money boosts stock fund assets to $2 trillion in May.

text.p: Investors poured a net $20.14 billion in new money into stock mutual funds in May, boosting the funds' assets to $2.019 trillion for the first time, said a report issued Thursday -- but analysts see the trend cooling off in the months ahead.
The Investment Company Institute, a mutual fund industry group, said the May inflow to stock funds represented the bulk of the $33.15 billion net new cash flow into the industry in May.
The stock funds' gain beat the group's earlier estimate of $18.5 billion in net stock fund flows for May.
In April, the net inflow to stock mutual funds was $15.71 billion.
"This is a phenomenal peak for equity funds," said Gavin Quill, marketing vice president at Scudder Funds. But he cautioned the surge may not be sustainable.
The stock funds' growth raised combined assets of the nation's mutual funds to $3.905 trillion, up from April's $3.729 trillion, it said. In April, there was an outflow of $5.86 billion.
The institute said money market mutual fund assets in the week ended June 25 rose to $967.84 billion from a revised $966.57 billion the prior week.

It said the assets of the nation's 664 retail money market mutual funds fell $546.4 million to $641.75 billion in the week. Of the retail funds, assets of the 403 taxable money market funds rose $566.8 million to $528.24 billion, while assets of the 261 tax-exempt funds fell $1.11 billion to $113.51 billion, the group said.

The trade group said assets of the 325 institutional money market funds rose $1.82 billion to $326.09 billion. Of these, assets of the 263 taxable money market funds increased $2.53 billion to $292.75 billion, while assets of the 62 tax-exempt funds fell $708.0 million to $33.34 billion, it said.
The institute revised total money market mutual fund assets for the previous week to $966.57 billion from $963.62.

Reflecting the recent highs in the stock markets, the flow into stock funds totalled $93.18 billion for the first five months of the year. That figure, however, was 24.6 percent behind the 1996 pace of $123.65 billion for the same period, the institute said.
For May, it said bond and income funds posted an inflow of $2.754 billion, raising the sector's net assets to $925 billion from $902 billion in April.
Money market funds had $10.26 billion in new money, compared with an outflow of $22.33 billion in April, due to withdrawals for payment of income taxes.
Quill said he expected "some moderation" in stock fund inflows for the rest of the summer, which has been traditionally slower over other months.
"We have already seen some moderation in June," he said, though he noted there were still "solid inflows across the board."
